- [Substack: Trump vs The Fed, U.S. Takes 10% Stake in Intel, Cracker Barrel Cracks | The Friday Market Wrap!](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/trump-vs-the-fed-us-takes-10-stake-cb0) - 2025-08-30

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

The August 29 wrap, uploaded August 30, combines Fed independence and government investment with a detailed tour of sector performance. Eisman links AI spending to semiconductors, power equipment and selected industrials while distinguishing operating quality from stock returns.

The sector disaggregation is useful. Several supporting descriptions are materially wrong: Equinix operates data centers, REITs do not distribute all cash, Mitsubishi is a major gas-turbine supplier, and Deckers is a footwear business. His Fed-removal prediction must be separated from the much narrower interim ruling.

<a id="youtube-62t_p65kbCw-c001"></a>
### 001. The Lisa Cook mortgage allegations are not proven criminal guilt.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 1:40-3:14](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=62t_p65kbCw&t=100s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The Court treated the allegations and procedural rights as contested, rather than as a conviction.

Assessment test: Separate allegations, evidence, charges and final adjudication.

- [Trump v. Cook stay decision](https://www.supremecourt.gov/opinions/25pdf/25a312_5468.pdf) (2026-06-29): The Court denied interim relief and required minimum notice and opportunity to respond. It protected the Fed for-cause framework but did not finally decide whether the alleged conduct supplied cause. Neither conviction nor indictment was made an automatic prerequisite.

### 005. The US is taking roughly 10% of Intel using previously allocated support.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

<a id="youtube-62t_p65kbCw-c009"></a>
### 009. Capitalization-weighted sector returns can conceal very different underlying company performance.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | analytical principle | major

[Source at 9:10-12:29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=62t_p65kbCw&t=550s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

An index return is the weighted sum of component returns; a large constituent can dominate a group despite numerous smaller winners.

Conditional reasoning: Portfolio return equals the sum of starting weights multiplied by component returns. Large weights can offset many smaller positive contributions.

Assessment test: Inspect weight times return and rebalance conventions.

<a id="youtube-62t_p65kbCw-c015"></a>
### 015. A better operating company need not have the best stock return over a given period.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | analytical principle | major

[Source at 16:06-16:37](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=62t_p65kbCw&t=966s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

Returns depend on the purchase price and changes in expectations as well as business results.

Conditional reasoning: A superior business purchased at a sufficiently higher multiple can underperform a weaker business whose results exceed a low initial expectation.

Assessment test: Compare beginning valuation, earnings revisions and total returns.

## Framework and tools

- Look inside capitalization-weighted sectors.
- Trace capital spending into suppliers and bottlenecks.
- Separate business quality from realized share performance.
- Treat legal allegations, findings and final remedies differently.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Sector weights and contribution
- Subindustry performance
- Data-center revenue
- Capital spending and REIT financing
- Registrations and autonomous rides

## Source cautions

Steve Eisman presents; speaker attribution follows the full dialogue.
- The episode says August 29 although the listing is August 30.
- Nvidia EPS is $1.05 adjusted; the $15 caption is not treated as his financial claim.
- A September 5 correction says he previously described Fed creation as a constitutional amendment; that wording is absent from this captured version, so it is not reconstructed as an August 30 claim.
